old: "Not until you let me kiss your hands! There! Enough! I'm getting up, and we'll go on! I'm a wretched fool, I'm unworthy of you, and drunk besides... and I'm ashamed.... I'm not worthy of loving you, but to pay you homage is the duty of every man who is not an utter beast! And I've paid homage.... Here are your lodgings, and for that alone Rodya was right to throw your Pyotr Petrovitch out! How dare he! How dare he put you in a place like this? It's outrageous! Do you know what kind of people they take in here? And you -- his fiancee! You're his fiancee, yes? Well then, I'll tell you -- your _fiance_ is a scoundrel."

old: "Well, so what!" Ilya Petrovitch drawled with gentlemanly nonchalance, swaggering over to another table with some papers, his shoulders swinging jauntily at each step. "Here, take a look if you will: this writer, or student — he was one at some point, at least — doesn't pay his debts, has given a promissory note, won't vacate his room, constant complaints are lodged against him, and then he has the nerve to protest about my smoking in his presence! He behaves like a cad himself — and just look at him, please. There's the gentleman, and what a fine sight he is!"
